userStories.title: Expose fleet requester names and thread titles on list and get
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add nullable requesterName/threadTitle to fleet job DTOs and enrich list/get with a module-wired batch reader.

**Motivation** — The jobs list and job detail print `people.nameOf(job.requestedById) ?? t('fleet.jobs.unknownMember')`, where `people` is the project member list, so every agent-requested job (10 live) reads "Unknown member".

**Approach** —
- `FleetJobDto` in `apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/dto/fleet-job.dto.ts`.
  - Target: it also has `requesterName: string | null` and `threadTitle: string | null` (both `@ApiPropertyOptional({ type: String, nullable: true })`, described 'Display name of the requester; null when the user or agent no longer exists' and 'Title of the thread the job was dispatched from; null when the job has no thread or the thread was deleted'). `FleetJobDto.from` sets both to `null`.
- New `apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/prisma-fleet-job-labels.repository.ts` (a repository file, since `.nax/rules/api-data.md` confines Prisma access to `*.repository.ts`).

It calls `readPrincipalNames` once with the jobs' requester ids, and issues one `chatThread.findMany({ where: { id: { in: threadIds } }, select: { id, title } })` with the non-null thread ids (no query when there are none). It is registered as a provider in `FleetJobsModule` and injected as its concrete class, with no token, as `PrismaTimelineRepository` is in `MemoryModule`: it is a read-only escape-hatch query, not an `AbstractPrismaRepository` aggregate.

- `FleetJobsService` constructor.
  - Target: a 16th, last parameter `@Optional() private readonly labels?: PrismaFleetJobLabelsRepository`, with `Optional` added to the `@nestjs/common` import. The six specs that call `new FleetJobsService(...)` with 15 arguments keep working, because the new parameter is last and optional.
- `FleetJobsService.list` and `FleetJobsService.get`. Target: each calls `this.labels.read` once with an array of `{ requestedById, threadId }` objects built from its row(s) (not the records themselves) and sets `requesterName` (from `names.get(requestedById)`) and `threadTitle` (from `threads.get(threadId)`, only when `threadId` is non-null) on the returned DTO(s), `null` when absent. With no reader injected, both fields stay `null`. Other routes that return a `FleetJobDto` (cancel, requeue, dispatch, config jobs) are unchanged and keep `null`.

Deduplicate thread ids; use `true` select flags for the selected id/title fields. Do not add deletedAt filtering to principal lookup. Any command with a threadId receives its thread title, not just THREAD. Do not put enrichment inside withPending or withDetail, since those are shared by routes outside scope. Preserve remapPage metadata, pending-approval counts, single-job tickets/configEdit, list summary omissions, and get's existing project-scoped lookup. No changes to requestedByType, stored feature, dispatch or transitions. Label database errors propagate without a catch.

 Run `bun run generate` from the repo root, and check that the regenerated diff carries only these fields.

**Scope** — In: DTO defaults/Swagger fields, concrete repository, provider wiring, last optional constructor argument, list/get enrichment, unit/DI/contract tests and generated artifacts. Out: shared reader implementation is US-001; web types/helpers/pages are US-005/US-006. Names on fleet job DTOs returned by cancel, requeue, dispatch and config-job routes: they keep `requesterName` and `threadTitle` `null`. The web reads names from the list and get routes only. A test for a failing label read: it propagates like any other repository error on those routes (no catch is added), so it needs no new handling.

**Interface** —
```ts
@Injectable()
export class PrismaFleetJobLabelsRepository {
  constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService<PrismaClient>) {}

  /** Requester names by principal id and thread titles by thread id, for one page of jobs. */
  async read(jobs: ReadonlyArray<{ requestedById: string; threadId: string | null }>): Promise<{ names: Map<string, string>; threads: Map<string, string> }>;
}
```

userStories.title: Centralize web fleet feature and requester labels
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add shared fleet display helpers, the web's THREAD/nullable label types and localized fallback labels.

**Motivation** — Fleet thread-turn jobs use `thread-<cuid>` as their feature name (F11).

**Approach** —
- `FleetJobDto` in `apps/web/lib/fleet-types.ts` gains `requesterName: string | null` and `threadTitle: string | null`.
- `FleetJobKind` in `apps/web/lib/fleet-types.ts` gains `'THREAD'`, which the API enum (`apps/api/src/common/enums.ts`) already has; without it `job.command === 'THREAD'` fails the web type-check.
- New `apps/web/lib/fleet-job-labels.ts`.
- `jobFeatureLabel`, in order: a config job (`isConfigJob`) -> `t('fleet.jobs.configFeature')`; a `THREAD` job -> `job.threadTitle` when it is a non-blank string, else `t('fleet.jobs.threadFeature')`; a `REVIEW` or `FIX` job whose `reviewPrNumber(job.feature)` is a number -> `PR #<n>`; every other job -> `job.feature`. This moves the logic that `featureLabel` (`pages/[project]/fleet/index.vue`) and `jobTitle` (`pages/[project]/fleet/jobs/[id]/index.vue`) duplicate today, and adds the THREAD branch.
- `jobRequesterLabel`: `job.requesterName ?? memberName(job.requestedById) ?? t('common.formerMember')`.
- i18n, in both `en.json` and `zh.json`:
  - New `common.formerMember`: en `Former member`, zh `已离开的成员`.
  - New `fleet.jobs.threadFeature`: en `Thread`, zh `线程` (the zh word `nav.threads` already uses).
  - `fleet.jobs.unknownMember` is left in place, unused.

Unused describes the completed feature: US-006 removes the existing page reads; this helper story keeps the locale key and does not edit either page's rendering.

Existing `isConfigJob` and `reviewPrNumber` are actually exported by `~/lib/fleet-jobs` in this checkout; reuse them there rather than inventing competing parsers in fleet-types. Return a non-blank thread title itself; use trimming only to detect blankness. Missing/deleted threads use the localized Thread fallback. An API requesterName short-circuits memberName; preserve the exact nullish precedence rather than truthiness. A PLAN/RUN job with a threadTitle still uses feature.

**Scope** — In: fleet-job-labels.ts, required web DTO fields, THREAD union member, two locale keys in both languages and pure helper tests. Out: API enrichment is US-004; removing the duplicated page logic and integrating helpers is US-006; home/timeline types and Ticket locale are US-007. Removing the now-unused `fleet.jobs.unknownMember` key.

**Interface** —
```ts
import type { FleetJobDto } from '~/lib/fleet-types'

type Translate = (key: string) => string

/** The feature cell and page title of a job. */
export function jobFeatureLabel(job: FleetJobDto, t: Translate): string

/** The requester cell of a job: the API name, else the project member name, else "Former member". */
export function jobRequesterLabel(job: FleetJobDto, memberName: (id: string) => string | null, t: Translate): string
```

**Tests** — Create `apps/web/tests/lib/fleet-job-labels.spec.ts` with THREAD populated/null/blank cases, existing review PR formatting, ordinary feature and config behavior, plus requester API/member/former-member precedence and the short-circuit spy assertion. Use the actual fleet-jobs helpers.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Integrate the real shared label helpers into both fleet jobs surfaces so THREAD titles and API requester names are visible.

**Motivation** — Fleet jobs requested by an agent, or by someone who left, show "Unknown member" (F11).

**Approach** — `pages/[project]/fleet/index.vue` and `pages/[project]/fleet/jobs/[id]/index.vue`. Target: the feature cell and the page title use `jobFeatureLabel(job, t)`; the requester cells use `jobRequesterLabel(job, people.nameOf, t)`. The `fleet.jobs.unknownMember` key is no longer read.

Use `jobFeatureLabel` and `jobRequesterLabel` on the jobs list page and the job detail page in place of `featureLabel`, `jobTitle` and the `people.nameOf(...) ?? t('fleet.jobs.unknownMember')` cells, as in Design. Remove duplicated title decision logic and unnecessary imports, not unrelated uses of isConfigJob. The detail page may retain a null-safe computed title adapter around jobFeatureLabel so PageHeader still sees an empty string before a job loads. Keep detail's configJob computed for its panels and action logic. Real helper behavior is config first, THREAD title/non-blank fallback, REVIEW/FIX canonical PR label, else feature; requester is API name, member name, then common.formerMember. No mocks replacing the imported helpers in integration mounts. Preserve non-THREAD titles, existing member-name fallback, codeLabel command rendering, horizontal scroll, routes, permissions, actions, live reload and filter behavior.

**Scope** — In: the two pages and their existing list/detail page tests. Out: helper/type/locale implementation is US-005; API enrichment is US-004; home/timeline display is US-007. Other surfaces that print a thread job's `thread-<id>` feature: `components/home/HomeNeedsYou.vue`, the fleet overview's `ActiveRunsTable.vue` and `RecentRunsList.vue`, and the job logs page. Only the jobs list and job detail page change here. Removing the now-unused `fleet.jobs.unknownMember` key.

**Interface** — Calls to upstream helpers: `jobFeatureLabel(job, t)` and `jobRequesterLabel(job, people.nameOf, t)` from `~/lib/fleet-job-labels`. DTO input fields are `requesterName: string | null` and `threadTitle: string | null`, supplied by list/get.

**Tests** — Add list AC-1/2 to fleet-jobs-list.spec.ts, using the existing mountSfc/fleet harness. Its fixtures gain requesterName: null and threadTitle: null. The test "the table scrolls sideways on narrow screens and names a requester who left" pins the source text `people.nameOf(job.requestedById) ?? t('fleet.jobs.unknownMember')`. That line is replaced by `jobRequesterLabel`, so the pin changes to the invariant that the requester cell reads `jobRequesterLabel(job, people.nameOf, t)`. The `overflow-x-auto` assertion stays unchanged. The test "S3 §6: config jobs show a readable feature without changing RUN/REVIEW/FIX rendering" pins the source text `if (isConfigJob(job)) return t('fleet.jobs.configFeature')`, which moves into the US-005 label helper; that pin changes to the invariant that the feature cell reads `jobFeatureLabel(job, t)`, and its `codeLabel(t, te, 'fleet.command', job.command)` assertion stays unchanged. In fleet-job-detail.spec.ts add AC-3 using the existing PageHeader stub exposing title and useProjectMemberNames stub; fixtures gain both null fields. Existing title/requester assertions stay unchanged: a non-THREAD job's title is still its feature, and a null requesterName falls back to the member name as before.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Render API actor names and ticket links on home activity and project timeline with localized former-member fallback.

**Motivation** — `components/home/HomeActivityList.vue` renders only the event type, the humanized action and the project slug.

**Approach** —
- `HomeActivity` in `apps/web/lib/home-types.ts` gains `actorName: string | null`, `ticketRef: string | null`, `ticketTitle: string | null`.
- `TimelineEvent` in `apps/web/composables/useTimelineEvents.ts` gains the same three fields.
- `components/home/HomeActivityList.vue`. Target, per row in this order:
  - the event-type label (unchanged);
  - the actor: `event.actorName ?? t('common.formerMember')`, in an element with `data-testid="home-activity-actor"`;
  - the humanized action, with the raw code as its `title` (unchanged);
  - when `event.ticketRef` and `event.projectSlug` are both non-empty strings (a truthiness check, so a fixture without the field, or the `''` slug `buildHomeView` falls back to, renders no link), a `NuxtLink` to `/${event.projectSlug}/tickets/${event.ticketRef}` with `data-testid="home-activity-ticket"`, reading `${ticketRef} ${ticketTitle}` (just the ref when the title is null);
  - the project slug and the age (unchanged).
- `pages/[project]/timeline.vue`.
  - Target: `actorName(event)` is `event.actorName ?? memberNames.nameOf(event.actorId) ?? agentNames.nameOf(event.actorId) ?? t('common.formerMember')`. A new Ticket column (header `t('timeline.columns.ticket')`) sits between action and when. When `event.ticketRef` is a non-empty string (truthiness), its cell holds a `NuxtLink` to `/${slug}/tickets/${event.ticketRef}` with `data-testid="timeline-ticket"`, reading `${ticketRef} ${ticketTitle}` (just the ref when the title is null). Otherwise the cell is empty.
- i18n, in both `en.json` and `zh.json`:
  - New `timeline.columns.ticket`: en `Ticket`, zh `工单`.

US-005 supplies common.formerMember (en Former member, zh 已离开的成员). Use text interpolation for names/titles, never v-html. Home does not add cross-project roster reads. Timeline keeps existing member/agent loads and silent roster-failure behavior, but never displays a raw actor id when all name sources miss. API names take precedence even if the current member roster names the same id differently. Missing tickets have no link; soft-deleted ticket links use the existing ticket page's not-found state, not new navigation/error handling. Fetch, filters, pagination, times and action humanization/tooltip remain unchanged.

**Scope** — In: home/timeline wire types, HomeActivityList, timeline page, three timeline test suites plus home component tests, both Ticket locale keys. Out: API enrichment is US-002/US-003; common fallback key is US-005; fleet pages are US-006; approval wording is US-008. Links for agent and decision events on the dashboard and timeline: those tables carry no ticket, and there is no page for one event.

**Interface** — Add `actorName: string | null`, `ticketRef: string | null`, `ticketTitle: string | null` to HomeActivity and the web TimelineEvent; timeline actorName now accepts a TimelineEvent rather than a string id. Link targets and test ids are exactly the ones specified above.

**Tests** — In home-activity-list.spec.ts extend event() with actorName: 'Alice', ticketRef: 'ACME-12', ticketTitle: 'Fix login'; keep its two existing tests unchanged and add AC-1 to AC-5. In timeline-readable.spec.ts extend row fixtures with null fields, resolve member/agent roster requests for mounts, map common.formerMember to Former member and timeline.columns.ticket to Ticket in the t stub, and add AC-6 to AC-10. Change the unknown-actor expectation from former-user to Former member while preserving humanized event/action and silent member-failure assertions. In timeline-agent-actor.spec.ts extend fixtures with null fields; the roster-rejection test must locate the agent event by row position, not raw agent-1 text, and expect common.formerMember because its t stub returns keys, retaining no-toast behavior. In timeline.spec.ts replace both event.actorId interpolation source pins with actorName(event) within the v-for; keep eventType/action pins unchanged. Extend its fixtures with null fields and change the SSR context stub from `(id: string) => id` to `(event: TimelineEvent) => event.actorId`, preserving user-1, agent-7 and admin in SSR output. Use mountSfc/uiStubs's NuxtLink representation to assert to/text rather than relying on a browser navigation.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Use translated or humanized permission labels consistently in approval UI and approval_request notification text.

**Motivation** — Toasts and the approval inbox already pass the key through `requestKeyLabel`, but only 2 of the 130 approvable keys have an `approvals.keys.*` label, and `requestKeyLabel` falls back to the raw key.

**Approach** —
- `requestKeyLabel(t, te, key)` in `apps/web/lib/approval-requests.ts`.
  - Target: the same label when the locale has it, else `humanizeCode(key)`.
- `components/approvals/ApprovalRequestInbox.vue`. Target: the key label span also carries `:title="row.permissionKey"`, so the raw key stays readable as a tooltip, as with every other `humanizeCode` use.
- `notificationText(n, i18n)` in `apps/web/lib/notifications.ts`. Target: for `n.kind === 'approval_request'` with a string `n.params.key`, the `key` param passed to `t` is `requestKeyLabel(i18n.t, i18n.te, n.params.key)`. Every other kind and param is unchanged.

The locale lookup remains `approvals.keys.<key with dots replaced by underscores>`. Reuse the existing humanizeCode implementation: fleet.flow.start -> Fleet flow start, memory.create -> Memory create. Copy notification params before replacing the display key; do not mutate persisted/received params or API titles. Keep unknown-kind title fallback and all other notification/detail/link behavior. Existing requestKeyLabel callers (toasts, inbox, HomeNeedsYou and JobApprovals) receive the fallback centrally; do not duplicate humanization at each call site. Preserve known translations such as approvals.keys.fleet_budget_override. Presentation only: do not change viewerActions, access checks, approval modes, policy, request creation, decisions or producer data. No API or schema changes.

**Scope** — In: requestKeyLabel fallback, raw-key label tooltip, notificationText's approval_request interpolation and affected existing web tests. Out: fleet label helpers/pages are US-005/US-006; actor/ticket rows are US-007. Locale labels for the 128 approvable permission keys that have none: the humanized key is the fallback. Adding `approvals.keys.*` labels is a separate copy task. The thread system note "Action <uuid> (koda_add_memory) was approved and done: memory:<id> saved" (F11). It is English text the agent reads, persisted in `ChatMessage.content`. Showing it readably needs structured message metadata, not parsing the English in the web.

**Interface** — Existing signatures stay unchanged:
```ts
export function requestKeyLabel(t: TranslateNamed, te: TranslationExists, key: string): string
export function notificationText(n: NotificationDto, i18n: NotificationI18n): string
```

**Tests** — Add AC-1/2 in tests/lib/approval-requests.spec.ts. The existing "AC-9: an unknown key stays raw" expectation for label.create becomes Label create; the known-key test stays unchanged. Add AC-3 in tests/components/approval-request-inbox.spec.ts. The unknown brand.new.key case now expects Brand new key as text and brand.new.key as the label's title, retaining raw-key visibility in the tooltip. Add AC-4/5/6 in tests/lib/notifications.spec.ts through the real requestKeyLabel and real en locale; change only the approval_request label.create matrix row to Approval needed: Label create, every other row stays unchanged. In tests/components/home-needs-you.spec.ts change the unlabelled approval key assertion (te returns false) from label.create to Label create. In tests/components/notification-bell.spec.ts change Approval needed: label.create to Approval needed: Label create. Preserve existing safe-link, unknown-kind and unrelated notification assertions.
